title: Fold and All-In: Two Key Poker Moves
summaryJa: 「フォールド」と「オールイン」はテキサスホールデムの最も重要な決断である。フォールドは手を降りることで、オールインは全てのチップを賭けることで、どちらも戦略的に使い分ける必要がある。
segments: Texas Hold'em poker has many important words. Two of the most common words are "fold" and "all-in.
" These words describe player choices at the table. Learning these words helps you understand the game.
Let me explain each one. "Fold" means to stop playing your hand.
You give up your cards to the dealer. You also give up any chips you put in the pot.
When you fold, you cannot win that hand. Why would a player fold?
A player folds when their cards are weak. They fold when they think another player has better cards.
Folding saves your money. For example, you have two low cards.
Another player bets big money. You think they have better cards.
You fold. You lose the chips you already put in.
But you save your remaining chips. "All-in" means you put all your chips into the pot.
You have no more chips at the table. When you go all-in, you bet everything on that hand.
This is a big and risky move. Players usually go all-in when they have strong cards.
They also go all-in when they want to make other players afraid. For example, you have two aces.
You push all your chips to the center of the table. You say "all-in.
" Now other players must decide. They can call you and match your chips.
Or they can fold. If they fold, you win the pot right away.
Fold and all-in are opposite moves. Fold means you quit the hand safely.
All-in means you risk everything on one hand. Good poker players use both moves at the right time.
They fold weak hands to save money. They go all-in with strong hands to win big pots.
Understanding when to fold and when to go all-in is very important for winning at Texas Hold'em.
